newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong minorities to get British passports.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong minorities to get British passports.

text.p: The British government on Tuesday bowed to pressure from members of parliament and from Hong Kong and said it would give passports to up to 8,000 ethnic minority residents of the colony, most of them Indian or Pakistani.

Home Secretary (interior minister) Michael Howard said he had carefully reviewed the position of ethnic minorities in the light of concern that their nationality would be uncertain after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
"It is clear that the assurances which they have been given over a number of years have not allayed this concern," Howard told parliament.

"I therefore intend to make provision enabling them to apply for registration as British citizens, giving them the right of abode in the United Kingdom after 30 June 1997," he said in a written answer.
Howard said he expected the great majority of those concerned to continue to live in Hong Kong.
The prospect of British citizenship, leaked in Tuesday's British press, was earlier welcomed by representatives of Hong Kong's non-Chinese population, who faced possible statelessness.
"If it is true, I'm absolutely delighted," Council of Hong Kong Indian Organisations chairman K. Sital told Reuters.

Ethnic minority representatives have always said their community members did not want to move to Britain en masse and had every intention of remaining in Hong Kong. But they wanted guarantees they would not be stuck in a stateless limbo.
Many of the Indians and Pakistanis affected have long ties with Britain dating back to the founding of the colony in the 1840s and have played a prominent role there since.
